Chapter 10: Sustaining the Practice—Lifelong Growth and Renewal
You know, just like any meaningful habit, praying the Bible isn’t always a straight line. There are going to be times when you feel excited and inspired—and other times when things feel a bit dry or even confusing. That’s totally normal. The real secret? Approaching the journey with patience, a whole lot of grace, and being open to change.
Let’s go through a few gentle reminders that can help you keep this practice alive, even when it feels tough.
First, embrace the seasons. Your interest and energy will naturally rise and fall. If you notice things getting a little stale, maybe it’s time to try a new book of the Bible, a different translation, or even just a fresh setting. And when your prayers feel full and rich, soak it in—maybe even share what you’re experiencing with someone else.
Next, don’t forget to return to the basics. If you ever feel lost or overwhelmed, go back to a favorite Psalm or a familiar passage. Let the simplicity of the process ground you and give you a sense of stability.
Another great way to keep growing is to invite others into your journey. Whether that’s a friend, a mentor, or even a small group, having someone to pray with can bring encouragement and accountability. It makes the whole experience richer.
And don’t overlook the power of celebrating growth. Take time to notice how your prayers, your attitude, and even your relationships are changing. Give thanks for the small steps and those moments of new understanding. Every bit of progress matters.
But above all, remember this: the goal isn’t perfection. It’s about relationship. The Bible is meant to be a lifelong companion—always ready to offer new wisdom, comfort, and insight, no matter where you are in life.
When you let Scripture become the foundation of your prayer life, you’re opening yourself up to ongoing growth, discovery, and real transformation. And that’s a journey worth taking, every single day.
